problems.title: Uncentered linearized sums used in mean-zero approximation
problems.evidence: ER_n(x)=-x sqrt(n) sigma_nb/2. Exact iid Gaussian ER_n(x)^2=n+x²n/4+x²(2b+1)/2-x²b(b+1)/(2n), contradicting (4.18); at x=1,mu=0 (4.20) tends to Phi(3/2)-Phi(2/sqrt5)>0.
problems.impact: Written principal normal-approximation proof invalid; smoothed raw moments have same centering defect. Intended centered CLT not disproved.
problems.repair: Center Y and sums, use variances/central cumulants, correct event comparisons and control nonstationary initial boundary. Subsidiary O(n^(2-a)) variance remainder should be O(1).
problems.counterevidence: Proposition4.10 already estimates centered covariance; correcting the local O(1) term fits later tolerance.

problems.title: Concentration block proof loses sqrt(b)

location.details: W_k definition, Lemma4.8, (4.30)-(4.31), final paragraph Lemma4.9

problems.evidence: For iid Gaussian and interior I_2b, centered W_k are orthogonal with EW_k²=4; L² norm of block sum=2sqrt(b), VarV_2b=2+4b, contradicting printed bound uniform in b.
problems.impact: Bounded-block input to concentration proof not established. Target sqrt(b/n) fluctuation scale not refuted.
problems.repair: Normalize centered blocks consistently and rederive sum, coupling and thresholds.
problems.counterevidence: Literal zero-origin coupling for iid positive blocks is zero; no false claim equating it with stationary relative-lag coupling.

problems.title: Uniform Edgeworth dependence hypothesis fails at allowed bandwidth
problems.evidence: Even granting stationarity/centering, iid Gaussian x=1 yields coupling c_q/sqrt(n) at lags1..b. Weighted norm asymp n^-1/2 b^(d+1) diverges at b=floor((n/log³n)^1/4) for every d>5/2. Smoothing alters only lag1.
problems.impact: Uniform Wasserstein proof input fails for allowed triangular array; correctly rescaled theorem not itself disproved.
problems.repair: New structure-aware uniform Edgeworth theorem or narrower bandwidth plus bias analysis; larger original a alone cannot fix.
problems.counterevidence: Ordinary Kolmogorov condition admits d between2/3 and min(1,a-3/2); this particular obstruction does not transfer to it.

problems.title: Theorem2.6 Gaussian comparison law has inverse scale
problems.evidence: Printed law G sigma_b/sigma conflicts with CDF Phi(x sigma_b/sigma). AR(1) rho1/2,varX1,p8,a5,b=floor(loglogn) satisfies all assumptions. With charitable positive floor, Gaussian quadratic-form/Lipschitz proof gives W1 to correct G sigma/sigma_b=o(2^-b), while wrong-target separation asymp2^-b≫n^-1/2. Complete analytic proof in exact report.
problems.impact: Principal quantitative assertion false as printed, even after favorable denominator completion.
problems.repair: Reverse ratio in named laws; separately repair P1-P3.
problems.counterevidence: CDF proof already uses correct reciprocal target; no claim intended theorem false.

problems.title: Nonpositive rectangular estimator lacks real-valued denominator completion
problems.evidence: iid {-2,0,2} with probabilities1/4,1/2,1/4; alternating0,2 sample at evenn oddb has probability2^(1-3n/2),Sn=n,Q=-1+(b+1)/n<0. Admissible odd growingb exists.
problems.impact: Statistic not defined on positive probability event; no claimed asymptotic failure of reasonable completion.
problems.repair: Specify bad-event real completion for Kolmogorov and sqrt(max(Q,tau^-2)) for Wasserstein.
problems.counterevidence: Asserted bad-event probability is of suitable order after concentration proof repair.

problems.title: Finite-window dependence inequality omits shifted coordinates
problems.evidence: Y_k iidRademacher,window2,f(u,v)=clip(v,-1,1),alpha1,beta0,Cf2,p=q6. X_k=epsilon_(k-1),lag1 LHS2^(5/6)>0 but current-coordinate RHS0.

checks.reason: The actual Y has mean summing to -x sqrt(n) sigma_nb/2. For iid standard Gaussians, Wick expansion with tr(W)=n and tr(W^2)=n(2b+1)-b(b+1) yields the stated raw second moment including x^2 n/4. At x=1 this contradicts the allowed O(sqrt(n)) error, and the probability limit Phi(3/2) differs from Phi(2/sqrt(5)). Mean-zero and stationarity requirements are genuinely absent for the defined initial-boundary variables. Later centered covariance is repair evidence, not an implicit earlier centering.

For the interior iid Gaussian block, W_k are orthogonal martingale differences with variance 4. Its length-b sum has L2 norm 2 sqrt(b), and adding the orthogonal diagonal monomials gives Var(V)=2+4b. This directly contradicts the printed uniform block bound feeding Proposition 4.6. Literal origin coupling can be zero and is not used as a false witness. The target fluctuation scale itself is not disproved.

Even after granting centered stationary replacements, replacing innovation 0 changes every Y_l for 1<=l<=b by -n^(-1/2) epsilon_l(epsilon_0-epsilon'_0). Thus the required weighted dependence sum is proportional to n^(-1/2)b^(d+1), diverging at the allowed maximum bandwidth for every d>5/2. Independent smoothing affects only lag 1. Iid Gaussian input meets arbitrarily strong original decay and moment conditions. The weaker Kolmogorov requirement permits d<1 and is explicitly not contradicted by this particular obstruction.

The CDF of G sigma/sigma_b is Phi(x sigma_b/sigma), opposite to the named theorem law. The stationary variance-one Gaussian AR(1), rho=1/2 and b=floor(log log n), meets all moment, dependence and bandwidth assumptions. Gaussian quadratic-form variance and the inverse-square-root Lipschitz bound show distance to the correct target is o(2^(-b)), even with a favorable real denominator floor. The two Gaussian target laws differ by a constant times 2^(-b), much greater than n^(-1/2). This is a principal quantitative statement counterexample; its short ratio repair does not reduce severity.

The admissible iid {-2,0,2} model gives the positive-probability alternating 0,2 event, sample mean 1 and Q=-1+(b+1)/n for even n and odd growing b. The square root is undefined as a real random variable; taking a maximum afterwards does not define it. A squared-estimator floor is an explicit reasonable repair, not proof every arbitrary completion retains Wasserstein control.

The bounded clipped second-coordinate map satisfies the global Holder assumption with alpha=1,beta=0. Iid Rademacher Y and a length-2 window yield X_k=epsilon_(k-1). At lag 1 its L6 coupling distance is 2^(5/6), while the printed current-coordinate distance is zero. The source does not redefine Y as the full window. Finite shifted dependence sums repair the local auxiliary inequality.

For centered Bernoulli(0.01), the zero atom at multiples of 100 has asymptotic mass [2 pi n*0.0099]^(-1/2). Any continuous CDF has essential-supremum error at least half this atom, with sqrt(n) limit lower bound greater than 2. Under the written common constant/common n range, q-th roots and q->infinity instead force error at most n^(-1/2). Bounded positive-floor statistics justify the Lq-to-Linfinity limit. This does not refute fixed-q rates or a distinctly stated q-dependent starting threshold.
